content:
AUTONOMOUS FULL-APP ENGINEERING + QA + LIVE DEPLOYMENT

Work autonomously across the complete application—not only the autonomous dashboard or selected modules.

SCOPE

Audit, repair, optimize, and verify every one of the 222 screens and all associated modules, routes, components, modals, tabs, forms, feeds, and navigation paths.

PRIMARY ISSUE

Some screens appear empty or frozen during normal use:

* Images do not visibly load after download/fetch.
* Text or posts do not appear.
* Clicking an item opens a module, but its content remains blank.
* Scrolling down does not load additional posts.
* Users receive no loading, error, retry, empty-state, or progress feedback.
* Updates do not appear in real time.

Apply one consistent, production-ready solution across all 222 screens.

IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

Use modern Instagram-style feed and media-loading techniques without copying proprietary code:

* Skeleton placeholders while content loads.
* Progressive image loading with low-resolution previews.
* Lazy loading using IntersectionObserver.
* Responsive image sizes and modern formats where supported.
* Image prefetching for likely next content.
* List virtualization and windowing for long feeds.
* Cursor-based pagination or infinite scrolling.
* Request deduplication and cancellation.
* Client-side caching with stale-while-revalidate behavior.
* Optimistic UI updates where safe.
* WebSocket, Server-Sent Events, or the project’s existing real-time subscription system.
* Automatic reconnect with exponential backoff.
* Clear loading, empty, offline, error, timeout, and retry states.
* Stable image aspect ratios to prevent layout shifts.
* Background refresh without replacing visible content with blank screens.
* Preserve the current scroll position during refreshes and navigation.
* Accessible keyboard navigation, focus handling, and screen-reader status messages.

Do not hide loading indicators before usable content is rendered. Do not return an empty container when a request fails.

TECHNICAL AUDIT

For every screen:

1. Trace its route, component tree, API requests, state management, authentication requirements, and media URLs.
2. Detect runtime exceptions, failed requests, authorization errors, invalid media URLs, CORS problems, race conditions, stale state, missing environment-variable bindings, pagination failures, and real-time subscription failures.
3. Repair shared infrastructure first, then screen-specific defects.
4. Consolidate duplicated loading/feed logic into reusable components and hooks where appropriate.
5. Preserve existing functionality and visual design unless a change is required to fix usability or accessibility.
6. Do not use mock data, simulated success, fake API results, or placeholder verification in production.

QA ALL 222 SCREENS

Create a machine-readable inventory containing:

* Screen number and name
* Route
* Module
* Authentication state tested
* Initial loading result
* Image-loading result
* Text/content result
* Click/navigation result
* Scroll/pagination result
* Real-time update result
* Empty/error/retry state result
* Mobile viewport result
* Desktop viewport result
* Console errors
* Network failures
* Final PASS/FAIL status
* Evidence reference

Test every screen at mobile and desktop sizes. Exercise real interactions: open, click, scroll, paginate, refresh, navigate back, reconnect, retry, and receive a real-time update where supported.

Automate repeatable browser tests using the project’s existing framework or Playwright. Add stable selectors only where necessary. Run linting, type checks, unit tests, integration tests, production build, and end-to-end tests.

EVIDENCE GATE

Never report a screen, deployment, GitHub operation, or test as successful unless it was actually executed and verified.

Before declaring completion, provide:

* Exact count: 222/222 screens tested
* Exact count of PASS and FAIL results
* Test commands executed
* Test output and exit codes
* Production build output
* Browser-test report
* Screenshots or traces for failures and representative successful flows
* Verified commit SHA from Git
* GitHub repository and branch
* Deployment provider
* Live production URL
* Deployment identifier
* Deployment timestamp
* Independent HTTP check of the live URL
* Post-deployment smoke-test results

Do not invent commit SHAs, logs, test results, screenshots, deployment IDs, or URLs. Clearly label anything that could not be executed as UNVERIFIED.

GITHUB OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL

The final source of truth must remain in my GitHub repository under my owner-controlled account.

* Work on a dedicated branch.
* Keep commits focused and traceable.
* Do not transfer repository ownership.
* Do not create an external repository as the canonical source.
* Do not expose secrets in source code, logs, screenshots, or commits.
* Use existing configured credentials and runtime variables.
* Push the verified changes to my repository.
* Provide the real branch name and commit SHA.
* Preserve rollback capability through Git history.

LIVE DEPLOYMENT

Deploy the verified production build using the project’s existing hosting configuration. Do not change providers or production architecture without a demonstrated technical requirement.

After deployment:

1. Open the live production URL.
2. Confirm the deployed commit matches the verified GitHub commit.
3. Repeat critical smoke tests against production.
4. Verify authentication, feeds, images, text, scrolling, pagination, clicks, navigation, and real-time updates.
5. Check browser console and network requests for production errors.
6. If deployment cannot be completed, report the exact blocker and raw error. Do not claim the application is live.

FINAL DELIVERABLE

Return:

* Implementation summary
* Root causes found
* Files actually changed
* Real Git diff summary
* QA matrix for all 222 screens
* Remaining failures or limitations
* Test and build evidence
* GitHub branch and verified commit SHA
* Live production URL and deployment evidence
* Rollback instructions

Completion is accepted only when all 222 screens have documented QA results and the live deployment has been independently verified.
